scenes.say: An app wants to read your calendar. The bad old way: you hand it your password. Now it can do anything, for as long as it likes.
OAuth replaces that with a short dance.

items.title: Redirect
items.text: the app sends you to the provider
items.say: The app sends you to the provider, say, your email service.

items.title: Consent
items.text: you approve what it asked for
items.say: You sign in there, and approve exactly what the app asked for.

items.title: Token
items.text: the app gets a limited key
items.say: The app gets back a token, a key that only opens what you approved.

scenes.say: The app never sees your password. It asks for a scope, like read-only calendar, and that's all it gets.

scenes.text:
Don't share the password.
*Share a key.*
scenes.say: You can revoke that token any time. That's OAuth. Don't share the password. Share a key.
